title: Formal-Methods Invariant Mining: Discovering What a Small Network Always Does

original_idea.body:
# Formal-Methods Invariant Mining: Discovering What a Small Network Always Does

**Problem:** ARC's agenda calls for formal mechanistic explanations that flag anomalous behavior on novel inputs, but discovering candidate invariants of a network by hand is slow and unprincipled.

**Direction:** Import Daikon-style dynamic invariant detection from formal methods. For a tiny algorithmic network (e.g., modular-addition or sorting transformer with public weights), instrument intermediate activations, run many inputs, and automatically mine likely invariants (linear relations, sign constraints, equalities among neuron groups). Then test whether out-of-distribution inputs violate the mined invariants — a cheap anomaly detector grounded in observed regularities.

**Why it matters:** Operationalizes ARC's call for formal mechanistic explanations and anomaly detection using an off-the-shelf cross-domain technique, on a model small enough to run anywhere. Anomaly-on-novel-inputs is a long-horizon theoretical concern that needs no lab resources.

**Relevant context:** Dynamic invariant detection (Daikon) infers likely program invariants from executions; invariant inference is used in neural-net verification (arXiv:2004.02462). ARC open problems: formal mechanistic explanations and anomaly detection on novel inputs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (invariant violation -> anomaly detection -> catch defection) but the link from toy-net invariants to catastrophic-risk reduction has a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: Daikon-style mining + tiny algorithmic nets is an inherited methodology a novice+mentor can execute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable (mine invariants, test OOD violation) with clear success criteria, few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: public tiny nets, no lab infra, ARC-style anomaly detection benefits from external work.

low_compute.reasoning: CPU/single-GPU analytical work on tiny nets.

novelty.reasoning: Invariant mining on nets exists but this anomaly-detection angle on tiny algorithmic nets may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Invariant mining on nets exists but this anomaly-detection angle on tiny algorithmic nets may be open.
